title: Tickeron weekly reach report, Nov 12–19, 2026
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
A full week of 577 original posts, scored by format, media, and time of day to see which posts actually get reach.

 

577Original postsFull week, no sampling

284Median impressions313.5 average

329Best median formatPremarket movers lists

4–8 PM PTBest time window305 median impressions

 

# What stood out

 

* Premarket movers lists had the most consistent reach, with a median of 329 impressions versus 284 for the week overall. That lead is even clearer if you set aside Thursday morning’s still-accruing posts, when the median rises to 345.
* Earnings recaps did not win on a typical post (median 277), but they produced the week’s biggest hit: the November 17 Nvidia beat-and-raise post reached 3,310 impressions, which is why this format has the highest average (357.7).
* Analyst price-target posts were the second-most common named format (91 posts) but underperformed, with a 275 median and the weakest engagement among the main formats (0.17%).
* X Articles reached a solid 309 median impressions but almost no interaction (0.08% engagement). They get seen; they rarely get a like or reply.
* The best posting window was late afternoon into evening Pacific time. Posts between 4 and 8 PM PT had a 305 median, and 6–8 PM was the strongest slice. Midday, from 9 AM to 1 PM, was the softest (median 267). Adding an image helped modestly: 301 median with media versus 282 without.

 

Most formats sit in a tight band around 260 to 330 median impressions, so a few breakout posts moved the averages more than the everyday template did. Engagement is light across the board at 0.26% (likes, replies, reposts, quotes, and bookmarks divided by impressions), which is typical for a high-volume market account.

 

**Thursday morning posts are still collecting views.**

29 posts from November 19, through 7:00 AM PT, are included but still accruing impressions (median 195, versus 286 for November 12–18). Format rankings look similar without them. Hedge fund 13F (8 posts) and macro / economic data (13 posts) are small samples.

Premarket movers lists (“Premarket movers: small/mid/large caps”) lead on median reach. Earnings recaps lead on average because of the Nvidia outlier. Analyst price-target posts (“What are the chances… reaches its Price Target,” “average of … analyst targets”) are frequent and relatively soft. Other includes head-to-head “which does AI favor?” comparisons, “links that explain” roundups, and one-off news posts.

119 posts (21%) included an image or other media. Posts with a link (232) had a slightly higher median (289.5) than posts without one (282), but a lower engagement rate (0.20% vs 0.30%).

All times are Pacific Time. The chart shows hours with at least 5 posts, so sparse late-evening and 1 AM slots are omitted. The 8 AM and 1 PM averages are pulled up by a few high-reach posts, including the Nvidia earnings recap at 1:30 PM PT on November 17.

Overnight posts, many of them X Articles around 2 AM, still get decent impressions (median 299) but almost no engagement. Midday is the weakest window for typical reach, especially 10 AM (median 259.5) and noon (258).
